svg.title: The German Revolution (Oct–Nov 1918), Armistice & Flight to Weimar (Jan–Feb 1919)
svg.desc: Historical GIS atlas map of Weimar Germany and neighbouring states (1918–19) illustrating the Allied North Sea naval blockade, the Wilhelmshaven and Kiel naval mutinies, revolutionary workers’ and soldiers’ councils across Hamburg and Munich, Kaiser Wilhelm II’s abdication at Spa HQ and exile to Amerongen, the 11 November 1918 Compiègne Armistice, the proclamation of the Republic and January 1919 Spartacist Uprising in Berlin, and the relocation of the National Constituent Assembly 250 km south-west to Weimar.

text.tspan: Kurt Eisner topples Wittelsbach king • Revolution spreads
Army abandons Wilhelm II • Abdication & Dutch exile
250 km SW of Berlin • Aug 1919 Constitution

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 3 (OPTION 31): WEIMAR & NAZI GERMANY, 1918–39
The German Revolution, Armistice & Flight to Weimar (Oct 1918 – Aug 1919)
Allied blockade starvation (750,000 deaths) & Kiel Mutiny (3 Nov 1918) toppled Wilhelm II (9 Nov) and forced the 11 Nov Compiègne Armistice.
Ebert’s pact with General Groener & Freikorps crushed the Jan 1919 Spartacist Rising, while deputies fled 250 km SW to Weimar to draft the Constitution.
